To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel method for deep neural network compression, CLIP-Q (Compression Learning by Interleaving Pruning and Quantization), that combines pruning and quantization, which are two complementary compression techniques.
we propose a new learning framework that jointly performs pruning and quantizaion, and that we show that this framework outperforms previous two-stage approaches.

(1) pruning and quantization are complementary, (2) pruning and quantizing jointly and in parallel with network fine-tuning is beneficial for compression, and (3) our CLIP-Q method achieves the state-of-the-art compression results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how to learn to prune a neural network and quantize its weights in a single framework, while preserving the accuracy of the original network?
the following question: how can we design a learning framework that enables us to learn the optimal trade-off between pruning and quantization?
the following questions: 1) How can we compress deep networks by jointly learning pruning and quantization in an in-parallel manner?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CLIP-Q is a new method for compressing deep neural networks by combining pruning and weight quantizations.
the CLIP-Q approach can compress a deep network to 1% of its uncompressed size with negligible accuracy degradation, and can be applied to a wide variety of network architectures.
the CLIP-Q method is an efficient and effective way of learning compressed networks by combining pruning and quantization, while maintaining the accuracy of the uncompressed network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel joint learning framework to perform network compression by combining pruning and quantization.
we propose a novel joint learning framework for deep network compression that outperforms the current state-of-the-art in terms of compression ratios and network accuracy.
CLIP-Q is an efficient and scalable method that can compress deep networks with high accuracy and can be easily integrated into existing training pipelines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pruning and quantization can be jointly performed in a single learning step.
a joint pruning-quantization approach is more efficient than the two-stage approach.
the two-stage pruning-quantization approach is not optimal, and a joint optimization of the pruning and quantization decisions leads to better results.
